conditions.name: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
conditions.summary: A common hormonal condition that affects how the ovaries work, often causing irregular periods and higher levels of androgen hormones.

conditions.name: Endometriosis
conditions.summary: Tissue similar to the womb lining grows in other places, such as the ovaries and fallopian tubes, often causing severe pain.

conditions.name: Adenomyosis
conditions.summary: The womb lining grows into the muscle wall of the womb. It mostly affects people over 35.

conditions.name: Uterine fibroids
conditions.summary: Non-cancerous growths in or around the womb. Many cause no symptoms; others cause heavy bleeding and pressure.

conditions.name: Heavy menstrual bleeding
conditions.summary: Periods heavy enough to affect daily life. It has several possible causes and is worth checking with a doctor.

conditions.name: Iron deficiency anaemia
conditions.summary: Low iron, often from heavy periods, which can cause tiredness, breathlessness and pale skin.

conditions.name: Common period pain (primary dysmenorrhoea)
conditions.summary: Cramping pain during periods without an underlying condition. It usually eases with painkillers and heat.

conditions.name: Premenstrual syndrome (PMS)
conditions.summary: Physical and emotional symptoms in the days or weeks before a period that ease once it starts.

conditions.name: Premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD)
conditions.summary: A severe form of PMS where mood symptoms seriously affect daily life before a period.

conditions.name: Missed periods linked to stress, weight change or exercise
conditions.short: missed periods from stress, weight change or exercise
conditions.summary: Periods can stop or become irregular after big weight loss, intense exercise or a lot of stress.

conditions.name: Possible pregnancy
conditions.summary: Pregnancy is the most common reason for a missed period. A pregnancy test can check.

conditions.name: Perimenopause or menopause
conditions.summary: Hormone changes as periods come to an end, usually between the ages of 45 and 55.

conditions.name: Early or premature menopause
conditions.summary: Periods becoming irregular or stopping before the age of 45, with menopause symptoms.

conditions.name: Ovarian cyst
conditions.summary: A fluid-filled sac on an ovary. Most cause no symptoms, but large or ruptured cysts can cause pain.

conditions.name: Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID)
conditions.summary: An infection of the womb, fallopian tubes or ovaries, often from an untreated STI. It needs antibiotics.

conditions.name: Bacterial vaginosis (BV)
conditions.summary: A common imbalance of vaginal bacteria that changes discharge. It is not an STI.

conditions.name: Vaginal thrush
conditions.summary: A common yeast infection that causes itching and thick white discharge.

conditions.name: Toxic shock syndrome (TSS)
conditions.summary: A rare but life-threatening reaction to bacterial toxins, linked to tampon and cup use. It is an emergency.

red_flags.message: Sudden, severe pain in your pelvis or tummy needs urgent medical care. Please call your local emergency number or go to an emergency department now, especially if you could be pregnant, feel faint or have a fever.
Feeling faint or fainting with heavy bleeding needs urgent help. Please contact emergency services or go to an emergency department.
A high temperature with a sunburn-like rash can be toxic shock syndrome. Take out any tampon or cup and get emergency help straight away.
If you could be pregnant and have pelvic pain, please get seen urgently to rule out an ectopic pregnancy.
Pelvic pain with a fever can be an infection such as PID. Try to see a doctor today.
